Package hadur2.core.memory

Class Tiers

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.memory.Tiers
public final class Tiers extends Object
The capability tiers a profile implies (the artifact's "Recognise, then adapt" tables), which the opening book turns into decisions at the first tick.

Each tier is read from an Estimate, and a tier is only named while that estimate's margin of error is at most MAX_MARGIN (DIAL-1). A wider margin leaves the tier UNKNOWN, and an unknown tier gets 1.20's defaults, so Hadur is never worse than 1.20 against an opponent it knows too little about.

The gun tier reads their normalised hit rate on us: each hit weighted by how small we looked from where they fired (the surf views' measure, Diamond's), so a rammer's point-blank hits do not make it look like a top gun. The movement tier reads our virtual guns' ratings, weighted the same way.

hadur2.core.adapt.OpeningBook reads both tiers once, at the first scan: the movement tier picks the first gun (ADAPT-1), gun tier T3 turns on the flattener (ADAPT-2), and the gun tier sets the starting distance. The power policy reads the gun tier too (POW-1 fires 3.0 against T0). All rates here are fractions, not percentages.

    • GUN_BOUNDS

      public static final double[] GUN_BOUNDS
      Gun tier boundaries on the normalised hit rate: T0 below the first, T3 from the last. The artifact's 4/9/14% were guesses; the S4 bench measured head-on sample bots under 2% and Shadow, a top learning gun, at 8.2% (normalised hits are a little lower than raw hits, as Hadur is usually far away). T1 and T2 are spaced between until the bench has mid-tier guns to measure.

    • move

      public static Tiers.Move move(OpponentProfile p)
      From our virtual guns' ratings: main at 25% or more is M0; both certainly under 10% is M3; the anti-surfer gun ahead of the main gun by more than the margin is M2; anything else M1.

      The order matters: a robot our main gun hits often is predictable (M0) whatever the anti-surfer gun does, and one neither gun can hit is a flattened surfer (M3) before the M2 comparison is made. M2 means the anti-surfer gun clearly does better than the main gun, the sign of a movement that adapts to where it has been shot at (a surfer, which ADAPT-1 answers with the anti-surfer gun).

      Parameters:
      p - the profile
      Returns:
      the movement tier, or Tiers.Move.UNKNOWN while either rating's margin is over 3 points

    • move

      Parameters:
